_comment: IAW status/bitfield decoders. 'enum' = value maps to one label; 'bits' = value is a bitmask, list every set flag. 'base' = radix of the keys. Attach to a param in params.json via {"map":"<name>","map_type":"enum|bits"} once the status-carrying rli is identified; the raw value is still logged.

motorstate._note: 0x58 read against 0x30/0x34/0x33 on 2026-09-05 (326 samples): only 0, 5, 6 and 7 ever appeared. 0x04 stands for as long as the engine turns and is the only bit left when it stops. 0x01 follows the throttle a sample ahead of 0x34 -- set while it sits at 1.7-2.0 deg, clear the moment it opens past 4.8 -- so it is the closed-throttle/idle condition, not a power state. 0x02 is a timer, not a temperature threshold: on 2026-09-08 it set 32 s after cranking began in both cold starts -- 09:53:09 -> 09:53:41 at 25 C and 18:59:03 -> 18:59:35 at 29 C, i.e. ~30 s after the engine caught, at coolant readings 4 C apart -- and never cleared. The 2026-09-05 reading (a single set as the coolant crossed 53->54 C) had only one start to look at and named it 'Warm-up done'. The three high bits were never observed here, so their meaning is still a guess and they are labelled as such. The old labels (0x01 'Power-On, engine OFF', 0x02 'Ignition ON, engine OFF') contradicted the data -- they were set with the engine running.

clutch._note: polarity verified on the bike 2026-09-04: the ECU answers 0 while the lever is pulled (the engine was started that way) and 1 with it released -- the reference table had it the other way round

runstate._note: 0x57 across 2026-09-09. 4 stands while the engine runs (732 of the 733 samples above 500 rpm) and the kill button takes it to 8, which the rider watched happen. 16 is the third value and the one still short of proof: it stood for two samples at the instant of one stop and arrived 18 s after another, which reads as the sleep the ECU announces to the bus once the ignition is gone. Labelled as a guess until a stop recorded with the ignition left on for a minute says otherwise.

kill_run._note: 0x7A and 0x79 are one input reported twice: strictly inverse across all 261 samples where both were read on 2026-09-09, with no (0,0) or (1,1) pair anywhere. 0x7A stood at 1 in every one of the 98 samples with the engine running, and its last flip to 1 landed in the same sample the starter pulled the battery to 7.9 V -- RUN set, then the button pressed. The rider confirmed the kill switch is what was being worked.

kill_stop._note: The other half of the same input, inverted -- see kill_run. Kept as its own channel because that is how the ECU answers it, and because the pair agreeing is the check that either is being read correctly.

lambda_ctl._note: 0x4B on 2026-09-08 (1130 same-state pairs), split by the sign of the 0x47 integrator step: 7 rises 266 times against 32 with the sensor at a median 175 mV (lean), 5 falls 200 against 35 at a median 727 mV (rich), and both carry 0x49 = 2 -- the two branches of the closed loop, 231 and 228 transitions between them. 4 is open loop with the integrator held (57 of 120 steps flat, 0x49 = 0), 3 is the same but transitional and rare, 1 is the controller frozen with the engine stopped (124 of 125 steps flat) and 2 only shows on a cold sensor (39-63 mV, integrator at 0). 0 and 6 were never seen, so they carry no label.

lambda_loop._note: 0x49 on the 2026-09-04 warm-up: a flat 0 for the first 43 s from cold, then 0<->2 at the rate the sensor itself switches -- 2 is the closed-loop correction being applied

idle_mode._note: 0x62 across the 2026-09-10 ride (693 samples): 0 only with the engine stopped, 4 only with the engine running and the throttle at its 1.6-2.0 deg stop (1168-2234 rpm), 2 everywhere else (1223-5053 rpm, throttle out to 25 deg). The three do not overlap, which is what the guessed label already said.

warmup_on._note: 0x5C is the on/off half of the correction 0x6A carries: (0x5C == 4) == (0x6A > 0) in 680 of 693 samples on 2026-09-10, and all 13 exceptions are single samples on a transition, where the two rli are answered one request apart. It had been labelled a closed-throttle switch, which the same ride refuted -- the throttle rule it was supposed to follow agrees on 92 % of samples at best, at any threshold and any lag.
